why_pinned: The sa1 base is vanilla/U with this patch applied, and its Reproducible pin describes the patched ROM. That hash is only meaningful alongside the revision that produced it, so the two move together: changing this file is what makes a new sa1/U hash legitimate rather than a regression. The patch's clean-ROM guards also fail open -- a guard that does not match skips its block and reports nothing -- so a partially applied patch assembles cleanly and produces a broken ROM. Pinning the revision is half of what stands between this base and that; vanilla/U staying byte-exact against a real cartridge is the other half.
why_this_revision: The working tree is 18 commits past the v1.40 tag and its changes.txt heads with 'SA-1 Pack v1.41', so v1.41 is in development and untagged upstream. The commit is therefore the identity and the ref is only a description of it. v1.41 is the revision that bumped the asar requirement to 1.90 and fixed I-RAM writes on boot that crashed accurate emulators -- which matters here, because Mesen is the core the editor embeds.
local_modifications: Five changes. The first three make a block's applicability say what it means rather than borrow a proxy, and all inert on a clean ROM. (1) asm/sa1.asm: !remap_dp and !remap_addr switches around the two work-RAM remap includes, defaulting to 1. (2) asm/sa1.asm: the $00:8A60 bank-switch block probes its own output rather than a byte remap/addr.asm rewrites. (3) remap/sprite_memory.asm: gated on !remap_sprite_memory rather than that same borrowed byte -- %remap_memory is idempotent by construction, so the clean-ROM probe was belt-and-braces. Everything else is verbatim. Intended for upstream: any base that relocates work RAM in its own source reads as 'already patched' to the borrowed probe and silently loses these blocks. (4) remap/map16.asm: the $05D89C rewrite stands down under Define_SMW_TranslevelRemap -- which the patch pass receives on its command line with the rest of the build's defines -- because that feature's JML occupies the read this patches and its own lookup already reads $40D000. Inert on a stock build. The overworld boost's literal seam at $048575 is instead honoured from the source side: the relocation feature pins an RTL at that address (Banks/Bank04.asm), so the boost runs unmodified over relocated builds. (5) remap/sprite_memory.asm: the bank each sprite list's header is patched in is read off the per-level table the managed level banks keep at the level bank's fixed tail (Define_SMW_LevelBank<<16|$FDFF) under Define_SMW_ManagedLevelMemory, because that feature packs sprite lists into whichever bank has room and the loader reads the same table; the stock $07 literal stands otherwise. Inert on a stock build.
why_modifiable: The Reproducible pin is what makes editing this tree safe: sa1/U must still assemble to produces_sha1, which was itself verified byte-identical to the patch applied to a real cartridge dump. An edit that changes behaviour changes that hash, and the gate fails.
migrated_to_source: remap/dp.asm and remap/addr.asm. Both halves of the work-RAM remap are placed by smw/src's own memory map, through !Define_SMW_DirectPageLocation and !Define_SMW_LowRAMLocation, and the patch's copies are switched off with !remap_dp=0 and !remap_addr=0. Each pair has to move together: a source rebase changes bytes those blocks' own guards probe, so leaving one on would have it skip half its work and report nothing.

differs_from_cartridge_by.summary: Four bytes, plus the checksum pair that follows from them. Everything else is byte-identical to SA-1 Pack applied to a real USA cartridge dump, which is how this pin was first established and remains the check worth making after any upgrade.

bytes.$05C666: cart $74, ours $14 -- the direct-page operand of `LDA.b $14`. With D=$3000 a direct-page access already reads $3014 and must not move; the patch relocates it to read $3074.
bytes.$05C672: cart $14, ours $74 -- the high byte of `STA.w $1464`, which the patch misses.
bytes.$05C6A8: cart $14, ours $74 -- the high byte of `LDX.w $1440`, which the patch misses.
bytes.$05C6AD: cart $14, ours $74 -- the high byte of `LDA.w $1446`, which the patch misses.

differs_from_cartridge_by.why_ours: All four are in SMW_Layer1SpecialScrolling05_Unused and SMW_Layer2SpecialScrolling06_Unused, which nothing calls. A community disassembly log renders both routines wrongly and the patch's remap tool inherits the error; this repository's reading was traced against the cartridge's bytes instruction by instruction. Nothing executes either way, so this is a correctness difference rather than a behavioural one -- but the pin should describe the more correct ROM.
